experiments.hypothesis: Finish exposed opponents using current ammo and time to turn, and route toward the selected opponent at useful weapon range.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests passed, 300/300 protocol, maximum 8.5 ms locally. No replay action differences. Recording contains no simultaneous opponents.
experiments.interpretation: New policy treated two exposed ranged contacts as enough to retreat and changed focus toward estimated finishes. No match traces identify a causal component.

experiments.hypothesis: Retain recently observed ground pickups and cubes across view loss to complete safe collection trips.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests, official protocol 300/300 locally, max 9.8 ms. Replay has 15 weapon reacquisitions but zero changed actions. Scenario tests exercise collection and abandonment.

experiments.hypothesis: Route to a walkable point shielded from a visible charging laser while zone travel is safe.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests, official checker 300/300 max 13.6ms locally. Replay changes 13 movement and 2 boost decisions, 0 aim or fire decisions.
experiments.probe: In a local ground movement model with recorded opponent positions, center and head were covered on the final step of 2/5 charge windows versus 1/5 for baseline. Enemy responses, damage and placement were not simulated.

experiments.hypothesis: A vetoed secondary yields torso control to the available gun to retain ordinary fire and movement lead. A held mortar previously suppressed both slots during a ranged retreat.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests passed, official checker 300/300 maximum 10.5ms locally. Scenarios verify close mortar, retreating mortar, low-energy arc and retreating laser. The supplied recording contains only a gun and no changed actions.
experiments.interpretation: The slot conflict is reproducible. Its fix can also spend ammunition or interrupt regeneration. The official service gives an aggregate score only, so the measured difference cannot be attributed to a specific cause.

experiments.hypothesis: Recover a missed secondary weapon en route into the next safe circle when the pre-shrink time budget covers both legs.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests, 300/300 checker maximum 11.0ms locally. Two recorded movement changes. Tests cover clock, route direction, view loss, contention and inner loot priority.

experiments.hypothesis: Move across the firing line during an isolated exposed duel at the stationary safe-zone goal. Existing navigation scores choose the open side, while cover and supply capture still permit holding position.
experiments.technical_validation: 40 tests and 300/300 checker, maximum 10.7ms locally. For 60 synthetic clear 95m duels on the official map, the baseline stopped in 60 and the candidate moved laterally in 60. Original recording unchanged.
experiments.ground_route_probe: 19 synthetic official-map positions, 2 seconds of ground movement. Median transverse displacement 0.0m baseline versus 22.52m candidate. 18/19 candidate routes crossed one mech radius, 0/19 baseline.
experiments.status: Official new best at 2.48, site selected.

experiments.hypothesis: Acquire the first secondary during a budgeted opening trip to a ground weapon or a breakable crate. Terrain height distinguishes hillside loot from rooftops. Recheck pressure, time and sight every decision.
experiments.technical_validation: 43 tests passed, 300/300 official checker, local max 12.5 ms, 21 movement changes on recorded input versus selected 2.48.
experiments.interpretation: Broader opening detours changed 21 recorded movements and regressed by 0.08. Extra travel and exposure are plausible costs. Match-level outcomes are unavailable.

experiments.hypothesis: Use a healthy, sufficiently energized lightning mech to close a short interval against one exposed laser carrier. Respect cover, supply capture, zone and pressure.
experiments.technical_validation: 44 tests passed and official checker 300/300 max 12.9ms locally. On ten synthetic official-map routes the selected baseline reached arc fire range in 0/10 and the candidate in 10/10 within three seconds. Median candidate first trigger was 1.4s. Opponent position held fixed.
experiments.interpretation: Closing on a laser opponent was effective at reaching arc range in the isolated scenario. The 48-match score fell. Exposure during approach or energy cost could explain the loss, but the official result does not identify which.

experiments.hypothesis: Use hit, damaged, HP loss and zone-entry observations to preserve imminent HP regeneration when a distant target is optional. Resume fire under pressure or for a finishing opportunity.
experiments.technical_validation: 43 tests passed, official checker 300/300 with an 8.6ms local maximum. Isolated firing tests cover ongoing combat, outgoing hits, zone re-entry, low enemy HP and laser response. Initial replay audit changed two fire decisions.
experiments.status: Official new best at 2.56, selected by the site.

experiments.hypothesis: Score visible imminent gun/NPC crossings with the observed velocity and permitted ground acceleration. Do not cancel an effective dodge merely because there is no current mech contact.
experiments.technical_validation: 46 tests passed, official checker 300/300 with a 17.0ms local maximum. Replay against 2.56 changes five movement decisions and zero other measured fields.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.56 parent. The crossing probe changed five recorded commands and improved clearance in a simplified model; its detours may cost firing position or interfere with other routing in matches. Cause unconfirmed without match traces. Next test is urgent obstacle routing on the 2.56 parent.

experiments.hypothesis: Seek nearby walkable shelter against a lone visible opponent only when the observed regeneration delay has elapsed or is about to elapse. Hold briefly while sheltered, release on damage or zone urgency.
experiments.technical_validation: 53 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 max 8.2 ms locally. Twelve recorded movement changes versus the selected 2.90 policy; all other action fields identical. Existing urgent path and torso attention behavior retained.

prepared_predecessors.technical_validation: 46 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 on time, maximum 9.4 ms locally. Twelve movement changes in 300 recorded observations, no aim or fire changes. No full-match local simulator.

experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.90. Holding a recently sheltered position or diverting toward it can interfere with pressure or subsequent movement. The official 48-match aggregate does not identify the cause. Retain fire discipline and test quiet field-of-view scanning next.

experiments.hypothesis: Route around walls that block urgent ground travel to the circle. Bounded A* runs across decisions. Following a verified detour permits temporary movement away from the circle while already outside; inside the current zone its border still applies.
experiments.technical_validation: 46 tests passed. Checker answered 300/300, max 10.6 ms locally, no recorded action changes. In synthetic ground routes around actual arena obstacles with a 14-second deadline, 18/24 reached the circle versus 7/24 without the planner. After freezing the policy, next eligible obstacles in map order gave 10/23 against 0/23. No match simulation or official score from these probes.
experiments.probe_sensitivity: With approximate axis-wise wall sliding and delayed energy regeneration, the planner reached 20/24 initial routes versus 7/24. On the additional 23 obstacle crossings it reached 10 versus 0. No opponent physics or match scores.

prepared_predecessors.official_submission_status: Validated, same game policy; no submission

experiments.assessment: Promoted after official evaluation. The 48-match practice mean increased by 0.09 from 2.56. The scorer does not identify which routes or matches produced that difference. Next test keeps this planner and isolates torso attention around cover.

experiments.hypothesis: When a lone in-range opponent is still tracked behind cover, keep its bearing in the front arc. Preserve stronger near/mid warnings or incoming damage from another direction. No firing into blocked geometry.
experiments.technical_validation: 50 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 with max 7.7 ms locally. Compared to the 2.65 winner, 57 recorded aim commands changed, with all other action fields identical. The behavior targets front-facing orientation while tracking a blocked contact.

prepared_predecessors.technical_validation: 47 tests, checker 300/300, max 6.7 ms locally. In 57 recorded observations of one occluded opponent the parent commanded 42 rear-facing orientations relative to the tracked contact; the candidate commanded zero. Only aim changed on replay. This measures commanded torso direction, not armor damage or official performance.

experiments.assessment: Selected by the official site. Against the 2.65 policy, this experiment raised the 48-match mean by 0.25. Changes to received damage, elimination count and individual placements are not exposed. Rebuild early-route and shelter experiments on this selected source.

experiments.hypothesis: Extend the verified 2.65 obstacle planner to quiet safe-zone travel before urgency when the next circle is still beyond the mech. Preserve combat, pickup pursuit and recent-damage response.
experiments.technical_validation: 51 tests. Official checker 300/300 max 7.8 ms locally. All 300 recorded commands matched the new 2.90 parent. The change affects quiet obstructed zone travel; synthetic route counts and preceding source are preserved in prepared_predecessors.

prepared_predecessors.technical_validation: 47 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 max 8.3 ms locally; no replay action changes. Synthetic early-circle traversals with approximate sliding on the official map: 20/24 initial and 10/23 additional crossings reached the circle within 14 seconds, versus 13/24 and 3/23 for the officially scored parent. No full-match results inferred.

experiments.assessment: Rejected by 0.02 against the 2.90 parent. Faster approach in isolated obstacle crossings did not produce a higher official mean. Earlier arrival can change exposure and loot timing. The scorer does not publish a per-match breakdown. Test regeneration shelter next and retain urgent-only routing.

experiments.hypothesis: With no engagement or recent warning, scan the least recently observed sector using actual torso facing and the published field of view, reducing the blind interval for initial detection.
experiments.technical_validation: 52 tests; checker 300/300 max 6.7 ms locally. Only aim changed on 39 recorded frames. In 72 stationary open-view cases (24 bearings, three starting yaws, published slew rate), average time until the bearing entered view dropped from 1.783 to 0.381 seconds and maximum from 7.1 to 1.1. Time to sight is a local geometry measure.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against 2.90. The faster open-field scan may spend more time facing irrelevant bearings or change initial engagements. The isolated visibility metric improved but the official aggregate decreased. Retain tracking of confirmed opponents and evaluate defense during weapon downtime.

experiments.hypothesis: While the only gun is reloading against multiple engaged shooters, use the front armor arc to cover more bearings and restore aim before the gun becomes ready. No change to active firing, movement or secondary attacks.
experiments.technical_validation: 55 tests passed. Official checker 300/300 max 6.5 ms locally, no recorded action changes; the starter recording lacks simultaneous opponents. Across eight fixed two-opponent reload scenarios with the official torso turn rate, rear-facing opponent-ticks fell from 200 to 50 and aim returned within floating-point precision when the gun was ready. No inferred match damage or placement.
experiments.assessment: Rejected against the 2.90 parent. The synthetic reduction in rear-facing bearings during reload did not carry through to the official aggregate. Actual opponents move during the reload and a torso turn can give up sensor coverage on the primary opponent. Cause unverified. Evaluate safe starter-drone encounters next.

experiments.hypothesis: Estimate how much recent opponent velocity persists at the current gun travel horizon, using only previously observed motion and a regularized estimate.
experiments.technical_validation: Local diagnostic only. Interpolated observed positions at projectile travel time. First 79 usable forecasts: mean horizontal error 4.025m versus 3.816m for constant velocity; within one radius 30 versus 33. Later 74 forecasts: error 2.141m versus 1.721m; within one radius 52 versus 58. Both segments favored the existing constant-velocity predictor.
experiments.assessment: Rejected locally before integration; keep the existing gun aim. No official evaluation or submission slot used.

experiments.hypothesis: Use the starter gun against a lone nearby drone when the current magazine can finish it and its two cubes are reachable in the future circle. An exposed mech or existing crate remains higher priority. Preserve recovery, zone travel and the magazine when the fight is unsafe.
experiments.technical_validation: 54 tests passed; checker 300/300 max 7.5 ms locally. Six controlled eligible drone scenarios yielded six aligned fire actions versus zero from the parent. A stationary full-health scenario completed eight hit updates without a mid-burst reload. The official recording contains no drones, and all 300 recorded actions matched the 2.90 source. No inferred match damage, cube count or placement.

experiments.hypothesis: Preserve banked progress during the last 1.5 seconds of a supply capture when the observed holder is ourselves, zone travel is safe and known opponents cannot immediately contest the ring. Keep existing combat and safe movement within its boundary.
experiments.technical_validation: 53 tests passed, official checker 300/300 max 7.0 ms locally. The official recording has no supply drops. Six controlled ground scenarios spanning three health values and two initial velocities completed six captures with the constraint versus zero with the parent behavior. This counts boundary crossings and simulated capture progress, not practice results.
